segments.english: §2. And all the more so we should not believe him when he says that Elijah was revealed to him, or the Elder of Elders, who is Atika Kadisha, which is called Keter Elyon (the Supreme Crown), for surely he is a false prophet, and his death is by strangulation. As is explained in the words of the Rambam in his commentary on the Mishnah, in his introduction to the Order of Zera'im. And in the Gemara, Pesachim 34, we read: "It was stated: the distraction of the mind. Rabbi Yochanan said: a disqualification by impurity, for if Elijah should come and declare it clean and say that impurity had not touched them, we listen to him; and Resh Lakish said: it is a disqualification of the body, for if Elijah should come and declare it clean, we do not listen to him." Thus far his words. And Rashi, of blessed memory, explains: "A disqualification of the body is a special feature in sacred offerings, in that they are disqualified by it; and there the disqualification is in itself; and even if Elijah should come and say that they were not defiled during all those days that he distracted his mind from them, we do not listen to him." Thus far. Hence, anyone who comes to change and to permit what is forbidden, even a rabbinic prohibition, we do not listen to him.

grammar: שלא נאמין לו: 'that we should not believe him', a clause with שלא and the imperfect after כ"ש, 'all the more so'.
סבא דסבין is Aramaic: 'the Elder of Elders', with the Aramaic relative ד and the title given as a name-like epithet.
The Talmud passage is quoted with 'גרס' (גרסינן, 'we read'); the closing 'עכ"ל' ends it, and 'ע"כ' ends Rashi's words after it.

שאם in the two rulings is explanatory, 'for if': Elijah's testimony is offered as the test of whether the disqualification is one of impurity or of the body. הסח הדעת is a noun phrase, 'the distraction of the mind'.
ויטהרנה: the verb with the object suffix -נה; the English 'declare it clean' takes the suffix as 'it'.
segments.note: The paragraph has three parts: the refusal to believe the claimed revelation, a Talmud passage with Resh Lakish's view, and Rashi's explanation with the conclusion. The Hebrew is the Wikisource base text.
apparatus: Base text: Wikisource edition, translated as base text and flagged until the 1931 scan is collated (decisions, Q2).
Rambam: his commentary on the Mishnah, introduction to Zera'im, as the author gives it (no chapter or page).
Pesachim (לד): the author's '34' as written; the quotation as he gives it, not checked against the Talmud text.
אמתר (3:1.37): printed word, not a word of the Gemara; translated 'It was stated' on the likelier אתמר (letters transposed); the alternative is the bare transliteration 'Amtar'.
רותן (3:1.92): printed word; translated 'those' on the likelier אותן, which the context requires ('all those days that he distracted his mind from them'); the alternative is 'their [unclear]'.
אלמלא (3:1.101): printed word ('if not for'); translated 'Hence' on the likelier אלמא ('so it follows'); with אלמלא the sentence has no main clause.
ושם (3:1.80) in Rashi: 'and there' (chosen) or 'and the name' ('and the name of disqualification is in itself').

segments.english: §3. And in truth, you began the words of your mouth with folly and wicked madness, in that you said: "How my heart emboldened me to inquire and to investigate, etc." And why not? On the contrary, the reverse is more reasonable (since they say to worship Ze'ir Anpin, who is created, Yosher Levav, folio 3b, and strength to God). It is a complete obligation upon us and upon each and every one of Israel to know the LORD, that He is Creator and not created, and to worship Him, as it is written: "And you shall know this day and take it to your heart." "And you shall know that the LORD your God is God, etc." And it says: "Know the God of your father and worship Him." And the Sages permitted restraining from the forbidden, even in the privy and in the bathhouse, for it is forbidden to meditate in them on words of Torah. And to restrain from the forbidden is permitted. And as to your astonishment, how could they err? There is no wonder in this. Nor is the sect of the later Kabbalists any better, those who went in their simplicity after the command of the philosopher, the author of the Zohar who attributed it to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, and Rabbi Eleazar his son, and his companions of the Great Sanhedrin who sat in the chamber of the Hewn Stone about whom Scripture said: "If a matter is too hard for you in judgment, etc." "And you shall rise and go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose, etc." "And you shall act according to the word that they tell you, etc." And yet, for all this, the Torah said that if the Great Court erred in a ruling and the people acted on their word, they bring an offering for their error. If they erred in idolatry and ruled, they bring a bull as a burnt offering and a goat as a sin offering, from each tribe. This is what is stated in the parashah of Shelach: "And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation it was done in error." And if in the other offences punishable by karet they erred and ruled, each tribe brings a bull for a sin offering. This is what is stated in the parashah of Vayikra. "And if all the congregation of Israel errs and the matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly."

tokens.note: ש: 'that'; the English drops it to give the sentence a main clause ('in truth, you began')
סכלות והוללות: echoes Eccl 10:13, 'folly' and 'wicked madness' (see apparatus)
רעה belongs to הוללות, as in Eccl 10:13 הוללות רעה
מלאני לבי: literally 'my heart filled me', the idiom of Esth 7:5 (מלאו לבו), 'dared me'
לז"א = לזעיר אנפין, 'to Ze'ir Anpin' (the Small Face, a Kabbalistic partzuf); first occurrence in this unit
יושר לבב: the title of a book (literally 'uprightness of heart'), cited here with a folio
ע"ב = side b of the folio
the author's spelling אלוהים for אלהים; 'to God'
לאפרושי: Aramaic causative infinitive, 'to cause to separate', i.e. to restrain (someone) from a prohibition; the object is not stated
בהם refers to the privy and the bathhouse
כת, 'sect', a group
האחרונים, 'the later ones'
הפילוסוף, the author's epithet for the author of the Zohar (decisions)
שתלאו, literally 'hung on'; the verb means to attribute
ב"ד הגדול = בית דין הגדול, 'the Great Court'
ע"ז = עבודה זרה, 'idolatry' (literally 'strange worship')
Shelach: the parashah of Numbers 13-15
כריתות: offences punished by karet
ויקרא: the parashah of Vayikra (Leviticus)

grammar: שהחלת דברי פיך סכלות והוללות רעה: echoes Eccl 10:13; 'folly and wicked madness' is what they began with, and 'שאמרת' ('in that you said') introduces the reader's own words.
איך מלאני לבי לדרוש ולחקור: the infinitives לדרוש and לחקור follow 'emboldened me'; the reader's question is closed by 'וכו'' and the author's reply begins with 'ולמה לא'.
ועוז לאלוהים sits in the author's parenthesis and no formula introduces it, so it takes no quotation marks; the parenthesis is kept as written.

לאפרושי מאיסורא: Aramaic causative infinitive, 'to restrain (someone) from a prohibition'; the author's point is that the Sages allowed even speech of Torah in the forbidden places to restrain from a transgression.
ואומר: 'and it says' introduces a verse; 'ועבדהו' is the verb 'worship' with the object suffix -הו, 'worship him'.
The conditional clauses (אם שגגו ... מביאים; ואם שגגו ... מביא) are built on perfects of 'to err' with present-tense apodosis, as the verses have them.
apparatus: Deut 4:39: 'וידעת היום והשבות אל לבבך', quoted with 'ככתוב'.
Deut 7:9: 'וידעת כי ה' אלהיך הוא האלהים', quoted with 'וכו''.
1 Chr 28:9: 'דע את אלהי אביך ועבדהו', quoted with 'ואומר'.
Eccl 10:13: 'תחלת דברי פיהו סכלות ואחרית פיהו הוללות רעה', echoed in 'שהחלת דברי פיך סכלות והוללות רעה' (an allusion, no quotation marks).
Esth 7:5: 'אשר מלאו לבו לעשות כן', echoed in 'מלאני לבי' (cf.).
ועוז לאלוהים in the parenthesis: no formula marks it, so no quotation marks; possibly Ps 68:35 ('תנו עוז לאלהים') or Ps 62:12 ('כי עז לאלהים'); not verified.
יושר לבב דף ג' ע"ב: a book title with the author's folio, as written; no text of the book is quoted here.
Deut 17:8: 'כי יפלא ממך דבר למשפט' and 'וקמת ועלית אל המקום אשר יבחר ה' אלהיך'. Deut 17:10: 'ועשית על פי הדבר אשר יגידו לך'. The author writes 'אלוהיך' for 'אלהיך'; the English follows the verse.
Num 15:24: 'והיה אם מעיני העדה נעשתה לשגגה'.
Lev 4:13: 'ואם כל עדת ישראל ישגו ונעלם דבר מעיני הקהל'.
לאפרושי (3:2.71, 83): read as causative, 'to restrain'; the alternative is the reflexive 'to abstain'.
context: The Hall of Hewn Stone (lishkat ha-gazit) is the chamber where the Great Sanhedrin sat, in the rabbinic account of the Temple; the author uses it to set the Sanhedrin against the circle he attacks.
